proposals.before: In the first year of Shengming, when Shen Youzhi rebelled, Inspector Chen Xianda raised troops in support of the court, and Dun was executed for his earlier complicity.
proposals.after: In the first year of Shengming, when Shen Youzhi rebelled, Inspector Chen Xianda raised troops in support of the court, and Dun was killed for his hesitation.
proposals.reason: Chinese 猶預 means hesitation/vacillation, not prior complicity; Dun was killed for indecision.

proposals.before: In the first year of Shengming, when Shen Youzhi rebelled, the inspector Chen Xianda raised troops in response to the court, and Dun was killed for prior involvement.
proposals.after: In the first year of Shengming, when Shen Youzhi rebelled, the inspector Chen Xianda raised troops in response to the court, and Dun was killed for hesitation.
proposals.reason: Chinese 猶預 is hesitation, not prior involvement.

proposals.before: Hui was fearful and alarmed, went to the Founding Emperor to apologize, and was immediately provisionally appointed advisory staff officer on the Heir Apparent's Central Army staff.
proposals.after: Hui was fearful and alarmed, went to the Founding Emperor to apologize, and was immediately provisionally appointed advisory staff officer on Shizu's Central Army staff.
proposals.reason: Chinese 世祖中軍 is Shizu (future Emperor Wu), not the Heir Apparent.

proposals.before: When the Heir Apparent acceded, Hui was transferred to Household Subordinate of the Heir Apparent, but did not accept.
proposals.after: When Shizu / Emperor Wu acceded, Hui was transferred to Household Subordinate of the Heir Apparent, but did not accept.
proposals.reason: Chinese 世祖卽位 is Emperor Wu's accession, not the Heir Apparent's.

proposals.before: He was transferred to central army staff officer on the Prince of Guiyang's Northern Expedition staff, served on palace duty alongside the future Emperor Wu, won Emperor Ming's personal favor, and thereby became close friends with the Heir Apparent.
proposals.after: He was transferred to central army staff officer on the Prince of Guiyang's Northern Expedition staff, served on palace duty alongside the future Emperor Wu, won Emperor Ming's personal favor, and thereby became close friends with the future Emperor Wu.
proposals.reason: Final 世祖 is Shizu/future Emperor Wu, not Heir Apparent; the idiomatic gloss mismatches the Chinese.

proposals.before: Tan had a handsome beard and whiskers and had old ties with the Heir Apparent, the Prince of Yuzhang.
proposals.after: Tan had a fine beard and whiskers and was on old terms with Shizu, then Prince of Yuzhang.
proposals.reason: Chinese 世祖豫章王 is Shizu as Prince of Yuzhang; literal wrongly calls him Heir Apparent.

proposals.before: When the Heir Apparent did not go west, Quan was appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gates and acted as administrator of Wu commandery.
proposals.after: When Shizu / the future Emperor Wu did not go west, Quan was appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gates and acted in the affairs of Wu commandery.
proposals.reason: Chinese 世祖旣不行 is Shizu, not Heir Apparent.

proposals.before: He sent Crown Prince Wenhuai and Prince Ziliang of Jingling to straighten their dress and pay the respect due their father's old friend.
proposals.after: He sent Crown Prince Wenhui and Prince Ziliang of Jingling to straighten their dress and pay the respect due their father's old friend.
proposals.reason: 文惠 is conventionally Wenhui, not Wenhuai.

proposals.before: Quan's father Mou had campaigned against Yin Yan and pacified Shouyang without harming anyone; the people were grateful and erected a stele to honor him.
proposals.after: Quan's father Kan had campaigned against Yin Yan and pacified Shouyang without harming the people; the commoners honored him and set up a stele shrine.
proposals.reason: Chinese 勔 is the same personal name earlier rendered Kan/Mian, not Mou.

proposals.before: Quan's father Mou had campaigned against Yin Yan and pacified Shouyang, harming no one; the people thanked him and erected a stele in his honor.
proposals.after: Quan's father Kan had campaigned against Yin Yan and pacified Shouyang, harming no one; the people thanked him and erected a stele in his honor.
proposals.reason: Same name 勔 should not be Mou.

proposals.before: Quan then replaced Wang Jian, Prince of Shixing, as Bearer of the Staff, supervisor of military affairs in Yi and Ning, and Governor of Yi, retaining his rank as general.
proposals.after: Quan then replaced Xiao Jian, Prince of Shixing, as Bearer of the Staff, supervisor of military affairs in Yi and Ning, and Governor of Yi, retaining his rank as general.
proposals.reason: 始興王鑑 is Xiao Jian (萧/蕭), not Wang Jian; 王 here is "prince" title fused wrongly in English.

proposals.before: In the first year of Yanxing he again commanded the Right Army.
proposals.after: In the first year of Yanxing (延興) he again commanded the Right Army.
proposals.reason: Source 廷興 is likely a corruption of 延興 (Yanxing), the Hailing/Ming transition reign.

decisions.reason: 猶預 means hesitation or indecision. The existing translation incorrectly makes Dun complicit in Shen Youzhi's rebellion.

decisions.reason: 勔 is Mian, as the chapter itself correctly renders 劉勔 in s0091. The proposal notices the inconsistency but replaces Mou with another erroneous reading, Kan.

decisions.after: Quan's father Mian had campaigned against Yin Yan and pacified Shouyang, harming no one; the people honored him and erected a stele shrine.
decisions.reason: The literal field must likewise render 勔 as Mian, not Mou or Kan.
In 始興王鑑, 王 is the title 'prince' and 鑑 is the given name of Xiao Jian. It does not form the personal name Wang Jian.

decisions.after: In Yanxing 1 (AD 494), he again commanded the Right Army.
decisions.reason: The received line's 廷興 is a textual error for 延興, as external editions attest. Supplying AD 494 resolves the reign year without inserting unexplained Chinese into the English translation.
